According to the black dots and solid lines that actually exist in the figure, the lowest noon solar altitude that actually exists throughout the year is 46°34′. Then reason: this place is located in the Northern Hemisphere, and the lowest noon solar altitude throughout the year occurs at the winter solstice. The formula for noon solar altitude at the winter solstice in the Northern Hemisphere is H=90°-(latitude+23°26′). Substituting H=46°34′ gives latitude=90°-23°26′-46°34′=20°, meaning this place is located at about 20°N. Around 20°N is often controlled by subtropical highs and dry trade winds, and is a common distribution belt of tropical and subtropical arid areas, so the most likely dryness and wetness characteristic of the climate at this place is arid all year round.
